question: Which level of government is primarily responsible for managing primary healthcare facilities in Nigeria?
explanation: Primary healthcare in Nigeria is managed largely at the grassroots level by Local Government Authorities with support from state governments. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h1)

question: What does the tertiary tier of the Nigerian healthcare delivery system typically consist of?

options.B: Teaching hospitals and federal medical centers

explanation: Tertiary care represents the apex of the system, comprising highly specialized teaching hospitals and federal medical centers managed federally. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h1)

question: What is the primary focus of care at primary health facilities in Nigeria?

options.B: Preventive, promotive, and basic curative care

explanation: Primary health facilities focus heavily on preventive, promotive, and basic curative health services at the grassroots level. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which cadre of healthcare workers typically leads the workforce in many Nigerian primary health facilities alongside nurses?
explanation: Primary health facilities are typically staffed and led by Community Health Officers (CHOs), CHEWs, midwives, and primary healthcare nurses. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is the primary operational role of secondary health facilities in relation to other tiers?

options.A: They act as the first point of contact for all rural populations
options.B: They function as referral centers for primary health facilities
options.C: They replace the need for tertiary teaching hospitals
options.D: They focus exclusively on community health education

explanation: Secondary health facilities serve as the middle tier, functioning primarily as referral destinations for cases coming from primary health facilities. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which government tier is primarily responsible for managing general and state hospitals in Nigeria?
explanation: State governments manage the majority of secondary health facilities through their Ministries of Health or Hospital Management Boards. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which of the following institutions is a characteristic example of a tertiary health facility in Nigeria?
explanation: University teaching hospitals and federal medical centers form the core of tertiary health facilities in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h4)

question: Aside from specialized patient care, what dual functions do tertiary facilities primarily fulfill?

options.A: Grassroots sanitation inspection and immunization tracking
options.C: Local government health budgeting and tax collection

explanation: Tertiary facilities serve as key centers for healthcare professional training (medical, nursing, allied health) and biomedical research. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary focus of social services when integrated with healthcare systems?

options.B: Addressing the social determinants of health and supporting vulnerable populations
options.C: Enforcing hospital financial policies and debt collection

explanation: Social services focus on addressing the social determinants of health, offering welfare support, and assisting vulnerable populations. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which professional within a healthcare facility typically assists patients with psychosocial assessments, financial counseling, and discharge planning?
explanation: Medical social workers assess psychosocial needs, offer financial counseling, and help coordinate discharge planning for patients. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is the purpose of a bidirectional referral pathway in the healthcare system?

options.A: To keep patients permanently admitted in tertiary hospitals
options.B: To move patients upward for complex care and downward for follow-up and rehabilitation
options.C: To eliminate the need for primary healthcare centers entirely
options.D: To restrict patient movement exclusively to private facilities

explanation: A bidirectional system allows upward referral for specialized care and downward referral for stabilization, follow-up, and rehabilitation. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is a major responsibility of nurses when managing a patient referral?

options.A: Providing personal financial loans for transport
options.B: Preparing accurate referral notes, stabilizing the patient, and communicating with the receiving facility
options.C: Designing the structural architecture of the receiving hospital
options.D: Purchasing medical equipment for the referral center

explanation: Nurses play a central role by stabilizing patients, preparing clinical handover documents, and communicating with the receiving team. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h6)

question: How do nurses primarily function when practicing in primary health facilities in Nigeria?

options.A: As sub-specialist neurosurgical intensive care nurses
options.B: As generalists, health educators, and community health leaders focusing on maternal and child health

explanation: At the primary level, nurses act as generalists and community leaders focusing heavily on preventive health and maternal-child care. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h7)

question: What is a notable administrative reality for nurses working in many primary and secondary facilities in Nigeria due to physician shortages?

options.A: They are prohibited from touching patient records
options.B: They frequently serve as administrative anchors and manage frontline triage and clinic operations
options.C: They automatically hold medical doctor licenses
options.D: They operate exclusively in private laboratories

explanation: Due to physician shortages, nurses often act as administrative anchors, managing primary clinics and making critical frontline decisions. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h7)
